messages:
aj: Heads-up — prototyping a tiered spot serving policy to shave GPU costs for nightly workloads while keeping interactive latency under 120ms. want quick feedback on thresholds and hunt for obvious failure modes.

maria: Nice. what's the high-level idea?

aj: Split workloads into 3 runtime tiers: A) interactive (strict latency SLO), B) warm batch (latency-sensitive background, checkpointable), C) long/off-peak transforms (cheap, preemptible). Strategy: prefer spot across all tiers, but enforce a small on-demand hedge for tier A and B to keep SLOs during interruptions.

liam: numbers? how big is the hedge?

aj: proposing a 10% on-demand reservation across regions for Tier A (auto-failover when spot interrupts). Tier B gets dynamic warm-pool sizing based on 10th-percentile concurrent interactive QPS * 0.2 (empirical). Tier C runs entirely on spot with aggressive preemption handling and checkpoint every 15m.

sam: where do off-peak shifts come in?

aj: Off-peak window 0200-0700 UTC: lower hedge to 2-3% and allow spilling of Tier B into larger spot pools to cut cost. During business hours bump to 12-15% if we see >3% observed interruption rate.

maria: eviction grace window? interactive requests can't just die.

aj: Plan: graceful eviction handler with 90s soft-grace for serving processes. Flow: detect provider preemption notice -> drain new requests -> flush KV cache -> forward in-flight request to on-demand fallback pool (if available) or serve a cached prediction with a de-escalation header.

liam: any changes to routing?

aj: Yes — smart routing policy prioritizes capacity by region/pool latency and preemption score. Basic policy: prefer local region spot, if predicted p99 latency + failover cost > target then route to on-demand. We'll expose a per-model policy flag: prefer_cost | prefer_latency | hybrid.

sam: can we see a sample config?

aj: sure: 
```yaml
policy_name: tiered_spot_v1
hedge_percent: 10 # for Tier A
warm_pool: {metric: interactive_qps_p10, factor: 0.2}
eviction_grace_s: 90
checkpoint_interval_s: 900
offpeak_windows: ["02:00-07:00 UTC"]
fallback_order: [spot_local, spot_other_region, on_demand_local, on_demand_global]
```

maria: we should limit on-demand burst to avoid bill shock. cap it at +20% of baseline on-demand footprint and add alerting when usage > 80% of cap.

aj: Agreed — will add a cooldown and billing guard. Also plan per-customer SLA flags: enterprise tenants get larger hedges.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: canary=5% of serving pool in us-west1 tonight 02:30 UTC — link: https://deploys/internal/12345 :rocket:

oncall-bot: FYI — scheduled maintenance in us-east1 03:00-04:00 UTC might reduce spot capacity.

liam: good catch — we'll exclude us-east1 from canary and bump hedge there to 20% during maintenance window.

sam: I'll run a synthetic load test tomorrow 09:00 UTC to exercise failover paths and measure p99 impact. want to capture latency impact, cost delta, and number of forced on-demand allocations.

maria: also add a tiny eval set with typical prompt prefixes so we can detect quality regressions if we switch model quantization or lighter variants during fallback.

aj: action items: 1) I’ll open a PR with the policy + circuit-breaker limits. 2) liam to size warm-pool autoscaler. 3) sam to run load tests and post results. 4) ops to add billing guard alert. 5) marketing note for enterprise hedges.

liam: ack, will prototyping warm-pool scaling based on recent telemetry (past 7d).

sam: ack — will share test dashboards.

maria: thanks — :eyes: — this will help cost a lot if it behaves.

aj: cool — PR incoming.
